articles.title: From bling and birds to ‘really fancy armour’ – the best dressed characters of the Bayeux tapestry
articles.summary: Medieval experts talk us through the fashion of the near-1,000-year-old embroidered work, and what it says about the characters wearing it. Don’t get Fashion Statement delivered to your inbox? Sign up here.
body: Blood, booze, arrows and boats; these are what you might typically imagine when you think of the Bayeux tapestry, which has become one of the hottest historical tickets since it went on display at the British Museum in London this month. But what about the hair?

“The Anglo-Saxons all have these little moustaches, which are brilliant. And then the Normans have these funny haircuts with the back of their heads shaved,” says Prof Laura Cleaver, an expert in medieval manuscripts at the Institute of English Studies.
And the clothes? There are crowns and tights, and brooches that wouldn’t look out of place anchoring one of Colman Domingo’s lapels at the Oscars.
The 70-metre-long embroidery – it’s famously not, in fact, a tapestry – was stitched almost 1,000 years ago and tells the story of the Norman conquest.

articles.title: Experience: a brain surgeon dropped part of my skull on the floor
articles.summary: I was a healthy 34-year-old when a mass of blood vessels ruptured in my brain. It took three neurosurgeons and a risky 16-hour operation to fix me. On a Sunday in May 2017, I was at the gym and using a chest press when there was this pop. It wasn’t a sound – it was more like a sigh in my body.
body: I ended up in A&E for hours at nearby St Thomas’ hospital in London. I was 34, healthy and had started regaining feeling in my leg, so they theorised it was a bruised spine and thought it was safe to discharge me. Overworked staff and shift changes meant that when MRI images of my brain went missing, nobody tracked them down.

At a follow-up appointment days later, my partner, Luke, argued with the consultant. I was still struggling to walk, and assuming I’d had a stroke caused by a blood clot, the consultant wanted to prescribe a high-dose blood thinner. However, Luke – an ICU nurse at the time – demanded a scan.

He saved my life. I returned from a CT scan to find the consultant looking pale: they had found a massive bleed on my brain and were sending me to specialists at King’s College hospital. Blood thinners might have killed me.

Tests confirmed an arteriovenous malformation (AVM) – a mass of tangled blood vessels – had ruptured close to the part of the brain that controls motor function in my limbs, causing a stroke. The consultant neurosurgeon and AVM expert rated it 4 out of 6 on the Spetzler-Martin grading system, which measures complexity, location and size.

articles.title: Benjamina Ebuehi’s recipe for Belgian buns | The sweet spot
articles.summary: These old-school classic treats may struggle for attention among today’s more Instagram-worthy cardamon buns, but they’re simple to make and divine to devour. Belgian buns are among a dying breed of bakes, forgotten about in favour of pretty cinnamon and cardamom buns and creative laminated doughs.
body: Put the flour, sugar, yeast and salt in a large bowl or stand mixer, and mix briefly to combine. pour in the milk, water, one egg, and the lemon zest, and stir until the mixture comes together into a shaggy dough. Knead by hand for eight to 10 minutes (or in a stand mixer for about five minutes), until you have a soft dough, then leave to rest uncovered for five minutes.

Pat the dough flat on a lightly floured work surface and smush the butter all over the top. Fold the dough over itself, then knead again; it’s a messy job, but use a dough scraper to scrape the surface often and it will eventually all come together. Once the butter is completely incorporated and the dough looks silky and shiny, put it in a lightly greased bowl, cover and leave to prove in a warm place for two to three hours, until puffy and nearly doubled in size.

Knock the air out of the dough, then tip it out on to a lightly floured work surface. Roll it out to a roughly 35cm x 25cm rectangle, then spoon the lemon curd on top and spread it out evenly. Sprinkle the sultanas all over.
points: These old-school classic treats may struggle for attention among today’s more Instagram-worthy cardamon buns, but they’re simple to make and divine to devour.

body: Welcome to The Scoop, a weekly email series in which I quiz fashion insiders on the stories of the week.

SIR. is one of those DTC brands that exploded in Instagram’s heyday, leading, in many ways, to the e-commerce reckoning of a few years ago. Sophie and Nikki are traveling to Paris next week to celebrate more than a decade in business, so I called them up for a chat.

Nikki: We’re gearing up for a big summer because we’re in Australia, and it’s also our brand’s anniversary celebration. We are about to launch our anniversary collection with a campaign we shot in Greece. Then, from September 30 to October 6, we will be in Paris with our first solo showroom space.
Nikki: We’ve shown a little outside of Paris before, but this time we will be in Rue de Thorigny, which is central and also our own space.

articles.title: “My Community Made It Happen”: Inside Mexican Brand Neithan Herbert’s Milan Debut
articles.summary: Mexican Ecuadorian designer Neithan Herbert Ruiz Pillajo built a solid yet modest business selling artisanal fashion in resort boutiques. Now, he’s ready for the Milan runway.
body: “I have good news, my atelier is coming with me to Milan,” says Mexican Ecuadorian designer Neithan Herbert Ruiz Pillajo, speaking over Zoom from his hometown, San Miguel de Allende. It’s one week out from his eponymous label’s runway debut at Milan Fashion Week on Saturday. When we last spoke over the summer, Ruiz wasn’t sure he could afford to bring the five Mexican women who weave, cut and sew his garments to Milan to be part of his show.

But when Ruiz’s creative community, many of them artists, jewelers and photographers, heard that Neithan Herbert was headed to fashion week but needed help with funds, they came together, donated their works and organized a fundraiser, so his artisans could join him. “I never expected it, but it was so beautiful,” the designer says. “It feels like the energies are aligning. My community made it happen.”
points: Mexican Ecuadorian designer Neithan Herbert Ruiz Pillajo built a solid yet modest business selling artisanal fashion in resort boutiques.

articles.title: Tempeh Is the Plant-Based Food With More Protein Than Eggs
articles.summary: Tempeh has two things going for it that many other protein-rich, vegetarian foods don’t: a ton of probiotics and all nine essential amino acids.
body: With all that, it’s surprising that so many people have yet to give tempeh a try. Below, a further look at all the reasons to include tempeh in your regular dietary rotation, whether you follow a plant-based diet or not.

Tempeh (pronounced “tem-pay”) is a cousin of tofu. But unlike tofu, which is made from curdled soy milk, tempeh is made from whole soybeans. Because of this, more of the legume’s nutritional properties—fiber, protein, vitamins—are retained.

Unlike tofu, tempeh is fermented, making it probiotic-rich. Thus, it has a deep, pronounced flavor packed with umami, which some people compare to hazelnuts. Traditionally, tempeh is made by fermenting whole black or yellow soybeans with the fungus Rhizopus oligosporus, and then compacting it into small loaves which are then wrapped in banana leaves to age. The technique gives the final product a dense, chewy texture.

Tempeh originated in Indonesia. According to our friends at Bon Appetit, its history “can be traced back 400 years (and possibly more than 1,000 years!) to the island of Java, where it holds great cultural significance.”

articles.title: Why Chefs Love Cooking on Stainless Steel
articles.summary: Stainless steel cookware is experiencing a cultural renaissance. This isn’t to say that the genre of cookware ever disappeared, but, once upon a lockdown, it felt like an ad from a nonstick cookware brand was always a scroll away.
body: If you buy something from a link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

So, why is virtually every commercial kitchen stocked with stainless steel cookware? Eater spoke with Carlye Lester, the sous chef at HAGS, a queer fine dining restaurant in New York City, about why she loves to reach for it at her restaurant, and so many other chefs and cooks do at theirs. The main benefit? Reliability. “I love that it gets super hot and heats evenly; it is [easy] to get a good sear on whatever you are making,” Lester says, explaining that she’s using stainless steel pans to sear and crisp a mustard marinaded-cod at HAGS. “[And] I love that stainless steel can be more reliable than a nonstick if you’re using the correct methods.”

That’s one of the greatest misconceptions about stainless steel cookware: that it is not nonstick. In actuality, if you heat up stainless steel cookware to the right temperature (around 400 degrees Fahrenheit, or once a few water droplets in the pan start beading instead of evaporating), and add a bit of oil, it creates a nonstick effect due to something called the Leidenfrost effect.

articles.title: 15 Vintage Pictures of the Divine Lisa Bonet
articles.summary: In September 1987, Lisa Bonet’s Denise Huxtable headed off to Hillman for her sophomore year—and 39 years to the day later, “A Different World” is officially back.
body: In September 1987, Lisa Bonet’s Denise Huxtable headed off to Hillman College for her sophomore year—and now, precisely 39 years later, the Cosby Show spinoff A Different World is back, with author, screenwriter, producer, and director Felicia Pride at the helm of the beloved NBC show’s brand-new Netflix revival.

Bonet may not be returning to Hillman’s campus just yet (though many of the show’s original cast, including Jasmine Guy and Kadeem Hardison, do reprise their roles, and Bonet’s character Denise is referenced…), but reflecting on the star’s turn as Denise has us reminiscing about the singular power of her bohemian, maximalist style throughout the 1980s and ’90s.
So here, we’ve gathered 15 jaw-droppingly chic vintage pictures of Bonet at the peak of her cool-girl powers… not that they’ve ever really abated.

articles.title: 11 Airbnbs Around the World That Are Practically Floating on Water
articles.summary: From overwater bungalows in Washington to hilltop hideaways in Greece, these Airbnbs are the ultimate blue escapes.
body: These listings were chosen by our editors based on Superhost and Guest Favorite status, amenities, location, previous guest reviews, and decor.

I stayed in this gem of an Airbnb in July, and have not stopped talking about it since. It sits on a hilltop in the Kalamaki settlement of Andros, an underrated Cycladic island that needs to be on everyone’s radar. The home gives you access to a semi-private beach that you share with another one of the host’s properties, as well as a garden where you can pick ripe tomatoes to enjoy in the shady outdoor kitchen and dining area. Best of all is the boundless view of the Aegean from both bedrooms, so blue it can bring you to tears.
